claims.text: Machine-learning prediction models can overcome current limitations in determining thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The intervention applies to high-temperature solid and liquid states over a large HEA compositional space.
Record W3201004060 developed machine-learning-based prediction models applicable to the proposed intervention.
Configurational entropy, mixing enthalpy, and Gibbs free energy mediate the effect of the machine-learning intervention.
Machine-learning models can learn relationships from existing HEA data and predict thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning prediction permits efficient exploration of HEA composition-phase space.
The proposed models can identify optimal alloys having desired properties.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of enthalpy and entropy of fusion relative to current methods.
The intervention will improve determination of volume change upon melting relative to current methods.
The intervention will improve determination of liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
The intervention will increase the availability and efficiency of thermodynamic-property determinations across a large compositional space.
Model accuracy depends on the quality and quantity of training data.
Model accuracy depends on the complexity of the underlying physical mechanisms.
Experimental high-temperature measurements of melting temperature, fusion quantities, melting volume change, and liquid properties can be used to test the predictions.
A significant deviation between predicted and experimentally measured properties would falsify the hypothesis.
